evidence_before.ctgrind: 771 errors across 9 contexts, all conditional jumps (5 je, 2 jb, 2 jae), no cmov, no address use

defect.statement: mod_exp_core looped `if limbs::bit(pd, i)`, so the secret exponent drove a conditional branch. BN_FLG_CONSTTIME was set by DH on its private exponent, but only BN_mod_exp_mont_word consulted it; BN_mod_exp_mont and BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime both called the branchy core.

allocation.failure_behaviour: forced malloc failure inside the ladder aborts the process (SIGABRT, exit 134, `memory allocation of 256 bytes failed`); there is no graceful error return. This is the recorded OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR divergence, not a new one.
allocation.structural: 7 allocations per ladder bit (two mont_mul calls with 3 allocations each, plus the ct_select result)

base.EC field_inverse_mod_ord: potentially secret: ecdsa_sign_setup inverts the secret nonce k; OPEN FINDING (initial limbs::rem is variable-time)
base.EC ossl_ec_GFp_mont_field_inv: potentially secret: field elements are not automatically public; OPEN FINDING
base.RSA private / CRT: public (ciphertext, or the encoded message being signed)

evidence_after.ctgrind: 0 errors from 0 contexts on the rebuilt DSO, modexp mode (ladder and output normalisation clean). Controls on the same DSO: CRYPTO_memcmp 0 errors, deliberate early-exit comparator 4096 errors from 1 context. BN_mod_inverse remains 620 errors from 209 contexts and is not part of this batch.

callers.DH (ossl_dh_compute_key, ossl_dh_generat: modulus p is public; exponent priv_key < p
callers.EC (ec_field_inverse_mod_ord via bn_mod_: modulus is the public group order; exponent order-2 is public
callers.RSA private / CRT (rsa_ossl_private_encr: modulus n (or p/q) has a public limb count; d/dmp1/dmq1 < it

width.public_source: modulus limb count (md.len()) at BN_mod_exp_mont, BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime and BN_mod_exp; the width-taking core also accepts an explicit declared_limbs for a caller whose exponent may exceed its modulus
width.residual: if an exponent's normalised limb count exceeds declared width, the ladder widens to that count (max) to keep the answer correct; the excess is observable. No reachable DH/RSA CRT/EC caller exceeds its modulus/order, so this fires only for an arbitrary C caller with an out-of-bound exponent.

non_claims: This is not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE or SAFETY_DISCHARGED promotion.
No timing-safety graduation is claimed; the residual normalisation site and the inverse remain open.
No attack or remote-timing claim is made.
not_established: the initial base reduction remains variable-time; DH and RSA bases are public, but EC field elements (notably ecdsa_sign_setup's secret nonce k through ec_field_inverse_mod_ord) are potentially secret. That is a live open finding, not a discharged obligation.
the constant-pattern trim removes the branch but not the length: the trimmed limb count of a secret result is still observable to whatever reads the returned BIGNUM, and it is value-dependent.

an exponent whose normalised limb count exceeds the declared public width widens the ladder to that count (max) so the answer stays correct; the excess length is then observable. No reachable DH/RSA CRT/EC caller has such an exponent.
an even modulus with a consttime flag deliberately stays on the variable-time path, because no Montgomery form exists for it
the new secret temporaries are not cleansed
ctgrind models data-flow branches and address use only
reachability from ssh/sshd of the named symbols is still may-bound; DH reaches the same core through BN_mod_exp_mont, which is what makes this reachable in practice

repair.design: fixed-pattern LSB-first ladder with 64 * public_width iterations, Montgomery REDC, and masked selection through the crate's existing constant_time_select; dispatch is explicit in BN_mod_exp_mont, BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime and BN_mod_exp (flag set, odd modulus). The loop width is the modulus' limb count (a public parameter) and never the exponent's normalised len(). The result is stored through a fixed-pass, mask-based trim (limbs::normalise_consttime / bignum::store_consttime) instead of the branching store. The variable-time path is retained for inputs their callers prove public.
repair.no_camouflage: no sleeps, no dummy work sized to mask; core::hint::black_box is not used as a constant-time mechanism
